ai.description: Brooke’s House Gecko reaches 5–6 cm snout-vent length. It is greyish-brown with dark dorsal blotches and has enlarged, keeled tubercles on its back and tail. Toe pads are expanded with divided lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus brookii* is best distinguished by its 16–20 enlarged, strongly keeled tubercles arranged in 16–20 regular longitudinal rows along the back.
ai.habitat: Brooke's House Geckos inhabit tropical deciduous forests, scrublands, and human settlements across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Brooke's House Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt insects near artificial lights where it remains highly alert to potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus brookii* is oviparous, laying clutches of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding in India typically occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus brookii* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level to 1,500m elevation in diverse habitats across most Indian states.
